problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨(t-6)^{2}{e}^{{t}^{2}-1},\,({t}^{2}-36)^{3}⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the time at which the particle is stationary. Do not round the answer.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}.

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡((t-1)^{2}+2),(t-1)^{3}⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the time at which the particle is stationary. Do not round the answer.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡((t-1)^{2}+2)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-1)^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2(t-1)}{(t-1)^{2}+2},\,3(t-1)^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =0 \\ ⟨\frac{2(t-1)}{(t-1)^{2}+2},\,3(t-1)^{2}⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(t-1)}{(t-1)^{2}+2}=0\, & ⇒\,t=1, \\ 3(t-1)^{2}=0\, & ⇒\,t=1.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=1$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations, so this is the only value of $t$ when the particle is stationary.
